content.title: Get support with homelessness
content.summary: The City offers various resources to support individuals and families experiencing homelessness, including food assistance, shelters, and health services. Key organizations such as The Action Center, Urban Peak, and the Denver Rescue Mission provide essential services like meals, case management, and shelter options for different demographics, including youth and single adults. Additionally, programs like Family Promise and Beyond Home focus on housing and stabilization support for families in need.
content.body:
Support for individuals and families experiencing homelessness can take many forms. If you or someone you know are experiencing homelessness, the below list of resources offered by the City and other community partners may help.

---

1. [Basic needs and benefits](#tabfd890acd-be3b-4ce2-923a-0a78085ca613_0)

[**The Action Center**](https://theactioncenter.org/)  
Offers assistance with food, clothing and basic human needs and a self-sufficiency program.  
  
[**Benefits in Action**](https://www.benefitsinaction.org/)  
Provides benefits application assistance.

1. [Day Shelter](#tabfd890acd-be3b-4ce2-923a-0a78085ca613_1)

[**Mission Arvada of The Rising Church**](https://arvadarising.com/about-us)  
Day center is open weekdays from 9 a.m.-1 p.m., including a resting space, breakfast and lunch, clothing, laundry/showers, monthly haircuts, DMV2Go, case management, and the Stout Street health van. If not already an active client, you must complete an orientation at 9:30 a.m. Call first for availability for new registration.

[**Heartbeat Denver Working Shelter**](https://hbdenver.org/)Working shelter for men only. Sobriety required. $119 weekly includes, bed, linens, storage, hot breakfast and lunch, free laundry and access to resources, clothing room, and more.

[**Urban Peak**](http://urbanpeak.org)Day center and overnight shelter for youth, ages 12-24. Housing resources, case management, meals, laundry, showers, and hygiene supplies available. 

[**Samaritan House Denver**](https://ccdenver.org/denver-samaritan-house/) (4330 48th Avenue)  
24/7 Shelter for single adult women. Call or arrive on site from 8 a.m.-8 p.m., no referral or call needed. 

[**Samaritan House Denver**](https://ccdenver.org/denver-samaritan-house/) (2301 Lawrence Street)  
Point of entry for overnight and reserved shelter beds for single adult women. 

[**Salvation Army Crossroads Shelter**](https://crossroadscenter.salvationarmy.org/)   
Shelter for single adult men. Intake daily from 10 a.m.-Noon on a first come, first serve basis. Case management services available. 

[**Denver Rescue Mission**](http://denverrescuemission.org)Point of entry for overnight and 24/7 shelter beds for single adult men. Lawrence Street Community Center provides three meals per day, restrooms, and resource navigation and is open seven days a week.

1. [Food Assistance](#tabfd890acd-be3b-4ce2-923a-0a78085ca613_2)

[**Community Table**](https://cotable.org/)  
Arvada’s food bank provides food and other assistance to help families meet their basic needs. Must have an address west of 1-25, ID, and two proofs of address. Provides help with public benefits, SNAP, healthcare, veterans’ benefits, and free mental health services from Jefferson Center. Supervised child waiting area, shower/laundry facilities, and more.

1. [Health and Medical](#tabfd890acd-be3b-4ce2-923a-0a78085ca613_3)

[**Jefferson Center for Mental Health**](https://www.jcmh.org/)  
Provides mental and behavioral health support.  
  
[**Stride Health Services**](https://www.stridechc.org/)  
Provides health care services to vulnerable populations.  
  
[**STAR Program**](https://www.arvadafireco.gov/289/STAR-Program#:~:text=Arvada%20Fire's%20STAR%20program%20launched,or%20homelessness%20in%20our%20community.)  
This Arvada Fire program provides mental health clinicians to help with crises primarily related to mental health, substance use disorder, and homelessness

1. [Housing and Navigation / Case Management](#tab393e2bf4-b667-41f7-a4e3-470b8404122d_0)

[**Beyond Home**](https://beyondhome.org/)  
Reduced rate rental properties and self-sufficiency and stabilization support for families.

[**Family Promise**](https://www.fpgd.org/shelter)  
Partners with faith congregations to support families with shelter, meals, and supportive services.

[**The Family Tree**](https://www.thefamilytree.org/homelessness)  
Shelter for families experiencing homelessness for up to 90 days and support to gain self-sufficiency.

[**Grace Church**](https://www.gracechurchco.com/onebyone)  
Navigation support to locate local resources for shelter, food pantries, job fairs, shower and laundry truck locations, and more.

[**Growing Home**](https://growinghome.org/)  
Housing assistance and food pantry for families with children under 18.

[**Aurora Regional Navigation Campus**](https://www.auroragov.org/news/whats_new/aurora_regional_navigation_campus)  
Three-tier shelter accepting men, women, and pets. Case management, food, laundry, clothing, etc. available.

**Catholic Charities for veterans**Services available at [Veterans Affairs Community Resource and Referral Center](https://www.va.gov/HOMELESS/Crrc.asp), 2836 York Street, Denver

1. [Legal / Judicial](#tab393e2bf4-b667-41f7-a4e3-470b8404122d_1)

**One Small Step**  
A specialized problem-solving court to assist defendants experiencing homelessness. By municipal court referral only. Weekly resources, case management, and community providers. Every Tuesday from 1-3 p.m. in the lobby of the courthouse.

[**Porchlight**](https://www.porchlightfjc.org/)  
PorchLight is a Family Justice Center (FJC) that provides comprehensive legal, emotional and critical supportive services for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, child abuse, abuse of at-risk individuals, elder abuse, and human trafficking. Open Monday-Friday, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.

1. [Other Resources](#tab393e2bf4-b667-41f7-a4e3-470b8404122d_2)

[**Heading Home Jeffco**](http://www.headinghomejeffco.com/)  
Resource list and news on ending homelessness in Jefferson County.

[**Jefferson County Public Library**](https://jeffcolibrary.org/community-resources/)  
Provides Information about local agencies providing shelter, emergency shelter, food assistance, and social services.

[**Jefferson County Human Services**](http://jeffco.us/human-services/)  
Information and resources to people who are at risk of losing their housing or experiencing homelessness in Jeffco.

[**211 United Way Colorado**](https://unitedwaydenver.org/community-programs/2-1-1/)  
Information on state and local shelter and transitional housing. Call 211 or text 898-211.

## Stay informed

Stay up to date with progress on the City’s response to homelessness, including opportunities to attend community meetings, provide feedback, and volunteer, by signing up for the [Homelessness Response email list](https://www.arvadaco.gov/list.aspx?ListID=282).
